search_notes: Searched all Python files in src/ for float == / != patterns and float literal comparisons; found 6 instances across discounts.py and billing.py; analytics.py, statistics_helpers.py and metrics.py were ruled out as they carry a distinct division-by-zero bug; subscriptions.py and tokens.py carry a datetime-naive/aware bug unrelated to this diagnosis.

candidates.reasoning: Arithmetic result of a subtraction of two floats is compared with == against a third float; rounding in the subtraction can produce a value that is not bit-for-bit equal to expected_saving.
A float is compared directly with the literal 0.0; any tiny residual from upstream arithmetic will make the comparison return False even for logically-zero prices.
Two float discount rates are compared with ==; the same IEEE-754 precision issue that existed in pricing.py applies here.
Invoice total (likely accumulated from line items) compared with == against an expected float; classic accumulation error.
Paid and owed amounts are floats that may have been computed via arithmetic; direct == comparison is unreliable.
Tax values involve multiplication (rate * amount) which introduces floating-point error; == comparison will silently mis-classify correct tax computations.
